- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots; cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% above peak.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.2) and price is rising, model underestimates continuation; add 2–3% to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; increase first 5 days’ forecast by 3–5%.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model delays reaction; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 82 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was negative 3–5 days ago, model often misses the 1–2 day lagged rebound; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment reversal.
